verses.text: These are the words of King Lemuel, a message his mother taught him:
"My son, my own son, the answer to my prayers!
Do not waste your strength on women, or on those who destroy kings.
Lemuel, it is not right for kings to drink wine. It is not right for rulers to want beer.
If they drink, they may forget what the law says and take away the rights of those who suffer.
Give beer to those who are dying and wine to those who are deeply troubled.
Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their troubles no more.
Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves. Defend the rights of all who are helpless.
Speak up and judge fairly. Defend the rights of the poor and needy."
Who can find a good wife? She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her completely. He has everything he needs.
She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.
She looks for wool and linen and works with eager hands.
She is like a merchant's ship, bringing her food from far away.
She gets up while it is still dark to provide food for her family and portions for her servant girls.
She looks at a field and buys it. With the money she has earned, she plants a vineyard.
She works hard and with energy. Her arms are strong for her tasks.
She sees that her business is going well. Her lamp does not go out at night.
She holds the wool in one hand and spins the thread with the other.
She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
She is not afraid of snow for her family, because all of them are dressed in warm red clothes.
She makes coverings for her bed. She dresses in fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he sits with the leaders of the land.
She makes linen clothes and sells them. She supplies belts to the merchants.
She is dressed in strength and dignity. She laughs without fear of the future.
When she speaks, her words are wise. She teaches with kindness.
She watches over everything that happens in her home. She is never lazy.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too:
"Many women do wonderful things, but you are better than all of them."
Charm can fool you, and beauty does not last, but a woman who respects the LORD should be praised.
Give her the reward she has earned. Let her works bring her praise at the city gate.
